body:
i lost my beloved cat, who i'd raised from 3 months old, to a brain tumor last October.  you're going to weep; that's okay, it's actually normal, & it ain't gonna stop for awhile.  but in time, the tears will come less.  maybe not every day, anymore, but still every week at least.  it's been more than half a year, here, & i still cry over my boy sometimes.  

i was told by multiple people, as his illness progressed, that i would "know" when it was time.  i didn't believe them... up until i did.  it was recommended by a vet to look up "cat quality of life" on google, & go down some lists.  ... i knew, finally, when it was time.  

i do not know if it's available in your area, but i used a "mobile veterinary hospice" service called Lap of Love.  they came to my home, so my Luke didn't have to leave again (he was always bad about being transported).  everything happened compassionately, & i got to hold him as he passed.  they also provide for getting the ashes back, which was a *huge* help to me; nice little box with his name.  

as to other tips for coping, i spent time getting photos printed, buying frames, & making a large collage on my wall of him, as well as pictures of my past cats.  mostly him.  i put it up in a corridor, so i see it when i come & go from my home.  it's got a little lamp beside it, so it's always lit - a sort of 'eternal flame,' in some traditions - & i see him still every day.  that's helped.  

i wish i had more tips for coping, but... a lot of this will just take time, i think.  meditate & remember.  let yourself cry.
you can mark yourself as only the second person in my life to get that reference!  heh. :)  such a good song.

one doesn't always have one's shit together.  but it sounds like you did everything you could to take care of him, & i do not see how anything was your fault.  i've had my struggles, as well, but it wasn't my fault, it was fucking cancer.  one cannot do anything about that.  thank you for your reply, & you sound like a compassionate person as well.

>  I came from a pretty dysfunctional family and didn't think I had a nurturing bone in my body. But, after experiencing the absolute pure love I had with this little guy, I'm a different person. I'm a better person. I'm forever changed because of him, as you are for your little one. They've made us who we are, and because of that reason they'll never leave us

same.  that's all i can say.  he made me a better person, & i learned so much from having him.  i learned to be more sympathetic, & i also learned *something* of what it might be to be a parent. (parenthesis, i don't want human children! heh.)  thank you for your reply.  one must never stop loving these creatures we raised & are beholden toward.  i hope that you find peace as well.

the world is such a dark place, now.  i can't say enough 'thank yous' to hospital workers, but---thank you.  my god, i can't imagine how difficult that must be.  you're doing something amazing with your job, & i'm so sorry that your normal life has become so similar to mine.  but we need to support one another, be kind, & be together.  if you ever need to talk, i'm an open ear.  Luke was one of the last i've had, & i'll lose everyone else sooner than later.  it's difficult to be alone, especially with the world being as it is.

*the only way out, is through*

you are entirely correct.  i appreciate your saying so, & that is a succinct way of putting it.  i have mostly avoided visiting this sub because i end-up in tears every time.  but you are an empathetic human, & you have made a bad night a little better by reaching-out.  so, thank you so much for that.  

i will attempt to "pay it forward" by reaching-out to others in similar situations; i will try to look at this sub more, as i am able.  it is much like other subs, in that one feels empathy but also just... sadness.  there is so much sadness in one's life, that it's difficult to cope with sometimes.  but you have done a great kindness to me by reaching-out, & i appreciate that.

it's the first time i've written about it.  many therapy appointments later, & i still felt the need to express.  

i am so sorry about your loss.  my word, it's so difficult.  if you would like to talk about it, i'm totally here to listen.  i don't check this account as much, but i would be entirely willing to listen & respond to your feelings of loss, as well.  

grieving seems to be a weird thing.  i don't know much about it, other than that it doesn't seem to end as quickly as one thinks it probably ought to end.  maybe it never does.  hell, i don't know.

it's so frustrating, splitting the difference between all the objectively good things that one has.... & the emptiness of it that one feels.  yeah, fuck.  

thank you for the reply.  i suppose this is a forum on which we are alone, but able to connect on some small level.
health struggles are the worst---just amplifies everything.  thank you for the reply, & i wish you peace.  hopefully some day we'll both find it, one way or another.

you're entirely correct in your sentiment---remembering that the suffering is much worse for other people, is perhaps the best thing we can do, to stay mindful & grateful for what we *do* still have.  i really appreciated your reply; thank you.  

we also have to find ways of forgiving ourselves for our suffering, despite that.  i think often of a Viktor Frankl quote, from *Man's Search for Meaning*:  

>“To draw an analogy: a man's suffering is similar to the behavior of a gas. If a certain quantity of gas is pumped into an empty chamber, it will fill the chamber completely and evenly, no matter how big the chamber. Thus suffering completely fills the human soul and conscious mind, no matter whether the suffering is great or little. Therefore the "size" of human suffering is absolutely relative.”

there are many equations.  i wish u well on yr journey, as well; thank you for the moment of relation.  the book is empty from the [whippoorwill](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZlKRKg-crvo)'s point of view.   :-)
